candidates.exact_span: Discharges from the facility may enter Lower Animas Ditch / Hampton Arroyo and/or Williams Arroyo in Water body Segment 20.6.4.98 / 99, with a critical low flow of 0 cfs. Discharges may also enter Water body Segment 20.6.4.404 or Segment 20.6.403 in the San Juan River Basin.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which receiving water(s) and segment(s) actually receive discharge, and whether critical low flow is 0 cfs versus a higher value, can change dilution-based limit derivation and biomonitoring/receiving-stream-dependent requirements.

candidates.exact_span: Previous permit identified the receiving water as a classified perennial stream, with a critical low flow (4Q3) for the Animas River, above Estes Arroyo as 184 cfs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether prior receiving-water classification and 184 cfs critical low flow still govern any part of FY2025 applicability, versus being superseded by the revised segments and 0 cfs value, can change which numeric limits and stream-dependent monitoring obligations are treated as applicable.

candidates.exact_span: Updated Minimum Quantification Level language in Part II of the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How MQL language is interpreted can determine whether reported values are suitable for numeric limit comparison versus report-only/no-comparison treatment, and how below-quantification or missing numeric results are classified.

candidates.exact_span: Biomonitoring test is changed from 48-hour Acute test to 7-day Chronic test based on updated critical dilution and updated receiving stream information.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the acute or chronic biomonitoring test (and its associated pass/fail criteria) applies changes both the monitoring obligation and the enforceable compliance standard used for comparison.

candidates.exact_span: TRC limit is changed from 0.019 mg/L to 0.011 mg/L based on updated critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which TRC numeric limit is operative (0.019 versus 0.011 mg/L) directly changes exceedance determinations for TRC measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Quarterly monitoring and reporting requirements for Cyanide total recoverable have been established in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether quarterly cyanide monitoring is an applicable obligation for FY2025 affects monitoring-applicability rows; absent cyanide results, it also affects whether missing data is unresolved required monitoring versus a documented non-applicable period.

candidates.exact_span: Monitoring and reporting requirements for Delta-BHC study have been established in the draft permit based on delta-BHC effluent testing data submitted by the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether and when the Delta-BHC special-study monitoring applies can change special-study obligation rows and how missing or non-routine results for that study are classified.

candidates.exact_span: This permitting action is for the discharge of backwash and flushing water originating from the potable water treatment plant.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Scope of regulated discharge (backwash and flushing water only) affects which parameters, limits, and monitoring requirements are considered applicable to reported measurements and to periods without results.

candidates.exact_span: The Water Treatment Plant (WTP) consists of four plants, operated separately, at the same location.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether obligations attach per plant, collectively, or to a single outfall can change which monitoring requirements are applicable and how missing evidence is attributed when plants operate separately.

candidates.exact_span: Two of the four plants go through a flush cycle with raw water approximately every four to five hours. Filter backwash using potable water occurs from once per day to once every three to four days depending on the plant and the time of year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Discharge-occurrence frequency that varies by plant and season can change whether event-dependent or periodic monitoring was required during specific FY2025 periods and whether no-data intervals reflect documented no-discharge/conditional non-requirement versus missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Samples are collected prior to discharge at the entrance to the pipe leading to the open channel to the Lower Animas Ditch.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The specified sampling location defines which measurements are treated as representative for compliance comparison and whether monitoring was required at that point versus another location in the discharge pathway.

candidates.exact_span: The sediment stockpile is tested using Toxicity Characteristic
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether sediment-stockpile toxicity testing constitutes a separate monitoring or special-study obligation (and on what schedule) can affect monitoring-applicability determinations and classification of any related non-routine or missing results.
